title: Lantern common definitions
description: Definitions shared by Lantern's documents (SPEC.md). Readers ignore fields they do not know; every document allows them.

schema1.description: The document's schema (SPEC.md § 3.2). A reader treats a higher one as absent.

platform.description: A platform's name (SPEC.md § 4.3): Atlas's where it has one (switch, steam, gog, xbox), and 3ds, vita, ps4, android, ios, windows, macos, linux, web.

id.description: A title or app id (SPEC.md § 6.1): opaque, of the form its platform's profile gives (Annex A), compared exactly.

id16.description: A Switch title or app id: 16 upper-case hex digits (SPEC.md Annex A.1).

switch_title_id.description: A Switch game's title id (SPEC.md Annex A.1): 16 upper-case hex digits, its lowest 13 bits zero.

switch_update_id.description: A Switch update's app id (SPEC.md Annex A.1): its game's title id plus 800 (hex).

app_type.description: An app's type, from its profile's list (SPEC.md § 6.1).

format.description: A package format, from its profile's list (SPEC.md § 6.1).

opaque.description: An opaque id or token, chosen by the server.

text.description: A string field (SPEC.md § 13: 4 KiB at most).

profile.description: The name a user gave a profile (SPEC.md § 9.1: 64 bytes at most); never a hardware or account identifier.

url.description: An absolute URL, or a path on the server's origin.

app.description: One installable package (SPEC.md § 6.1). On a Switch, its ids, type and format follow Annex A.1.

version_code.description: An integer, as the profile derives it: clients compare it, never version_name.

sha256.description: Of the file as served (SPEC.md § 6.1). Required: a server hashes a file before it lists it.

installed_size.description: The bytes it takes once installed, when the server knows them (SPEC.md § 6.1, § 6.3).

image.description: An image (SPEC.md § 7.1). external: elsewhere than the server's origin, never sent credentials.

genre.description: A genre, from SPEC.md § 7.1's fixed list. A reader shows one it does not know as other; the schema lists today's.

title.description: What the server knows about a game on one platform (SPEC.md § 7.1).

device_path.description: A path on the device (SPEC.md § 8.2): absolute, parts separated by /, none empty, . or ..; no backslash, colon, quote or control character; a part 255 bytes at most.

homebrew_id.description: A homebrew's id (SPEC.md § 8.1): reverse-DNS, lower-case, stable.

arch.description: A package's architecture (SPEC.md § 8.2): aarch64, armhf, x86, x86_64, riscv64, or a later one of the same form, which a reader that does not know it treats as not its own.

data_path.description: Where a port's required file goes, relative to the port's root (SPEC.md § 8.6): parts separated by /, none empty, . or ..; no leading /, no drive letter, backslash, colon, quote or control character.

required_data.description: A file a port needs from the user's own copy, or a group of alternatives (SPEC.md § 8.6); never served.

manifest_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the manifest's canonical form (SPEC.md § 8.2).

path.description: A single file's place on the device; absent when the system's installer installs it.

arch.description: The architectures it runs on (SPEC.md § 8.2); absent: every one of its platform.

signature.description: In packages only: this package's own signature (SPEC.md § 8.4).

signer_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the platform's own signing certificate, where the profile has one (SPEC.md § 8.2, Annex A.5).

package.description: A homebrew's package (SPEC.md § 8.2). A listing leaves manifest out.

homebrew.description: A homebrew (SPEC.md § 8.1). A listing leaves package.manifest out (§ 8.2).

system_id.description: The platform's own id of the installed software, where it has one (SPEC.md § 8.1, Annex A).

kind.description: What it is (SPEC.md § 8.1): app, game, port, emulator, tool, overlay, sysmodule or theme. A reader reads one it does not know as app.

genres.description: Genres, from the titles' fixed list (SPEC.md § 7.1, § 8.1): meant for a game or a port.

category.description: Gone in draft 0.3: shelves come from kind and genres (SPEC.md § 8.1). A server does not write it.

assets_license.description: The licence of the assets it bundles, when it differs (SPDX, LicenseRef- allowed).

packages.description: More packages of the same build, each for its arch (SPEC.md § 8.2).

cheat_set.description: A set of cheats for a game's build (SPEC.md § 10).

slot.description: One of a title's save folders (SPEC.md § 9.1), as the platform names it.

required_file.description: A file a port needs from the user (SPEC.md § 8.6).

port.description: A game port's original game, engine and data (SPEC.md § 8.6).

license.description: Only when it differs from the entry's.

data_root.description: An absolute folder, ending with /, under the profile's areas for ports' data (SPEC.md § 8.6): parts as in a device path.

assets.description: included, demo_included, free_external or user_owned; a reader reads one it does not know as user_owned.

3ds_title_id.description: A 3DS game's title id (SPEC.md Annex A.2): 16 upper-case hex digits, 00040000 (a game) or 00040002 (a demo) first.

3ds_app_id.description: A 3DS package's id (SPEC.md Annex A.2): its game's, an update's (0004000E) or an add-on's (0004008C).

vita_title_id.description: A Vita title id (SPEC.md Annex A.3): nine upper-case letters and digits.

vita_content_id.description: A Vita add-on's content id (SPEC.md Annex A.3).

ps4_title_id.description: A PS4 title id (SPEC.md Annex A.4): four upper-case letters and five digits.

ps4_content_id.description: A PS4 add-on's content id (SPEC.md Annex A.4).

android_package.description: An Android package name (SPEC.md Annex A.5).

profile_ids.description: The forms of title_id and app_id on the draft profiles (SPEC.md Annex A.2 to A.5), for any document that carries platform and those ids. The Switch's are given where its documents are.

dotted.description: A dotted version, compared part by part as numbers (SPEC.md § 8.7).

requires.description: What the device needs (SPEC.md § 8.7). min and gpu are conditions a client checks before it offers a package; a key it cannot read gives a warning, not a refusal. A server keeps the keys it does not know.

min.description: The lowest the device may have: the profile's keys (Annex A) as dotted versions, and glibc, ram_mb and screen, which any profile may use.

gpu.description: Graphics interfaces, at least one of which the device must offer. A later version may add names; the schema lists today's.

atlas.description: A game's id in Atlas (SPEC.md § 6.1): its Wikidata item, the key of Atlas's links.json. A hint, never an identity.

ratings.description: Age ratings, each an organisation's short name and its rating as it writes it (SPEC.md § 7.1); rating caps read them (§ 5.6).

rating_cap.description: A rating cap a token carries (SPEC.md § 5.6): an age, or a rating of one system; unrated says what becomes of what has no rating the table reads.

device_key.description: A device's public key, made at pairing (SPEC.md § 5.4): Ed25519, its 32 bytes in base64.

short_fingerprint.description: A key's short fingerprint (SPEC.md § 5.3): 16 upper-case hex digits in groups of 4.

invitation_code.description: An invitation's code (SPEC.md § 5.5): 16 to 32 symbols of the pairing alphabet, in groups of 4.

account_name.description: An account's name (SPEC.md § 5.7): 1 to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.

admin_user.description: An account, as the administration API shows it (SPEC.md § 5.7). No password, nor its hash.

admin_device.description: A paired device and its token, as the administration API shows it (SPEC.md § 5.7). Never the token, nor its hash.

admin_pairing.description: A pairing waiting for approval (SPEC.md § 5.7). Its id is not its poll address.
